items.title: 生活待购与灵感收藏夹

scenario.name: 生活待购与灵感收藏夹
scenario.audience: 习惯先把感兴趣的网页存起来、之后再回头处理的普通网络用户
scenario.objective: 把偶然看到但当下不处理的外部网页链接留存，日后需要时能重新找到并回到原页面
workflow: 用户在浏览时看到想记住的商品页、教程或灵感图片，主动保存该链接
保存时选择一个简单归类，如“待购”“家居改造”或“以后看看”
未经整理的链接可先进入默认归类，之后再手动移动到更合适的位置
用户在需要实际处理时打开个人库，浏览或检索相关归类
用户从记录打开链接，回到原始网页继续购买、阅读或参考

capabilities: 保存收藏（URL 必填，标题/描述可选）
默认“未整理”与预置归类集合
归类管理（新建/重命名/删除）
关键字检索（标题/域名/描述）
打开原始网页（URL 锚定与回跳）
多会话持久化（跨重启保留）
本地应用外壳与首启（空库）
limits: 不实现云同步、多用户共享或托管部署（D11、F16、F21）。
不保存网页快照、不做正文全文检索、不做失效链接检测（F17、F18、D13）。
不引入置顶/归档、多排序模式、复制 URL 与访问计数（F20、F23、F24）。
归类为扁平单选，不支持嵌套层级或多标签并存（F19、D01）。
第三方元数据与图标抓取未验证可达性，仅作可选增强且失败静默降级（F12、D05）。
验收不携带认证凭据；若目标要求认证，验收必须显式报告基础设施未就绪而非跳过或通过（D09）。
不设置未经验证的性能或成本目标。

runtime.scope: 保存、分类、移动、检索、打开链接、失败恢复、刷新与同目录重启；辅助首版，未覆盖完整严格错误矩阵。

items.title: 月有度 · 个人极简月度预算

scenario.name: 个人极简月度预算：先查剩余再消费
scenario.audience: 希望用预先承诺约束日常开支、且不连接银行账户的个人用户（如刚独立生活的年轻上班族）
scenario.objective: 为一个月的各项用途预先设定计划金额，并在每次消费前查看该用途的剩余额度，让计划真正影响消费决策。
workflow: 新建本期（月度）计划，为食品、房租、交通、娱乐等用途创建分配项并填写计划金额
登记本期可用的预期收入，检查各分配项计划金额之和是否超过收入
消费后手动录入一笔支出并归属到对应分配项，该分配项剩余额度随即减少
购买前打开计划页，查看相关分配项及整体的剩余额度，据此决定是否购买或缩减金额
月中某分配项即将用尽，从其他分配项转移金额，或让超出部分留在该分配项上形成超支
期末查看各分配项的计划、实际与剩余对照，未使用金额留在本期，并按模板数值开始下一期计划

capabilities: 月度计划、收入与精确金额
分类转移、月份隔离和模板
limits: 辅助试用；正式场景仍draft，不冒充发布或严格G1/T08。
上游未运行；共享案例证据独审pending。
完整财务/并发/多用户/导出矩阵后置。

runtime.scope: 预算、支出、精确金额汇总、修改后重算、月份隔离及重启持久化。

items.title: 会后 · 项目会议笔记

scenario.name: 多项目会议结论的归档与回查
scenario.audience: 同时跟进多个项目、以桌面端为主的职场人士
scenario.objective: 把会议结论和项目细节持续记入个人笔记库，按项目归档并管理活跃与过期笔记，使任一历史记录都能被可靠取回
workflow: 会议中用快速捕获窗口记录要点，先不决定归属
会后在桌面端把该笔记移入对应项目笔记本，并补充表格形式的决策与行动项
把当前重点推进的笔记置顶，使其在列表中始终可见
按阶段把已结束的笔记归档，清理活跃视图
把确实不需要的笔记删除，必要时在保留期内恢复
需要回顾时按容器浏览项目笔记本，找不到时改用全库搜索

capabilities: 置顶、归档与可恢复清理
limits: 辅助本机单用户；不声称G1/T08通过。
无附件/语音/团队/云同步/计费。
独立证据审阅pending，上游运行not_run。

runtime.scope: 项目隔离、正文保存/编辑、正文检索、归档恢复、刷新及同目录重启。

刷新及同目录重启后继续盘点

归档恢复与错误零写入

本批仅模板和验收程序，应用未实现/未运行

issues: acceptance/probe.py:157-164 (A01): before is captured before the successful PATCH at line 161, but line 164 compares the home after the empty PATCH to before. The home object includes updated_at (VIEW_ARCH.md:32; probe.py:155); a correct PATCH that refreshes updated_at makes the final zero-write check fail even though the empty patch wrote nothing. Use the patched response from line 161 as the baseline or compare only id/name/address.

acceptance/probe.py:171-175 (A01) tests blank name and unknown home but never an invalid category; AUTHOR_INPUT.json acceptance[1] and REVIEW_SCOPE.md:35-37 explicitly require invalid categories to return 422 or 404 with no equipment row, and VIEW_ARCH.md:38 defines the enum. Add an invalid-category POST and assert 422 plus an unchanged equipment list.

VIEW_ARCH.md:11 and :77 state a backdated completion never moves next due backwards, but max(previous last_completed_on, completed_on) + interval_days has no floor when last_completed_on is NULL (a plan created with only first_due_on or no anchor). Example: first_due_on 2026-03-01, interval 30, completed_on 2025-01-01 gives due_on 2025-01-31, earlier than 2026-03-01. probe.py:230,245-247 only backdates after a prior completion. Define an anchor floor or narrow the invariant and add the missing case.

acceptance/probe.py:197-210 (A02) checks selected task IDs and statuses but never the exact set or count; AUTHOR_INPUT.json acceptance[2] and REVIEW_SCOPE.md:40-42 require exact overdue/due/upcoming sets at the boundaries. Extra tasks, for example from earlier cases in the same disposable database, would not fail the probe. Assert the full ID set or count, preferably with a fresh equipment-filtered query.

acceptance/probe.py:311-313 (A05) only checks token presence (label, form, button, aria-live, and words); VIEW_ARCH.md:158-162 also requires label for/id linkage, fieldset/legend, caption, th scope=col, role=status, and lang=en. Token presence does not verify the stated accessibility rules; add structural assertions.

items.title: Home Care Ledger

scenario.name: Home Care Ledger
scenario.audience: A single homeowner keeping care records for their own home on a local machine, with no accounts, notifications, or multi-property operation.
scenario.objective: Create the home and its equipment, define every-N-day care plans anchored to them, see exactly which tasks are due or overdue as of a date, record a completion with a note, advance the next due date from the actual completion date, and retrieve care history by home or equipment.
workflow: Start the local server against a disposable data directory; initialize the SQLite schema on first start.
Create the single home with POST /api/home, then add equipment records with POST /api/equipment anchored by home_id.
Create care plans with POST /api/plans using interval_days and an optional equipment anchor.
Query GET /api/tasks/due with an explicit as_of and horizon_days to see overdue, due, and upcoming work.
Record a completion and note with POST /api/plans/{id}/completions; the same transaction updates the plan next due date.
Read GET /api/plans/{id}/completions or GET /api/history filtered by home_id and equipment_id.
Use GET / for the basic accessible single-page UI; all actions remain available through the documented JSON API.

limits: 辅助试产，非严格G1/T08。
Upstream status: not_run. The repository was read as evidence only; no build, test, server, TUI, or database was executed, so no upstream behavior is runtime-verified.
Runtime verification is not_run for the target too. The probe and architecture are authored artifacts; no server was started and no acceptance case was executed in this task.
Single-home and single-user by design; no multi-property, accounts, authentication, sharing, or remote access.
No notifications, email, SMS, push, calendar sync, or background scheduler; due work is pull-based through the API and UI.
No costs, vendors, receipts, photos, manuals, warranties, projects, quotes, incidents, documents, or LLM features; those upstream surfaces are intentionally out of scope.
Every-N-days recurrence differs from upstream interval months; no compatibility with upstream databases, APIs, or schema is claimed.
No delete, undo, archive, or restore endpoints; completion history is append-only and test records remain until the disposable data directory is discarded.
Validation is strict and date-only; natural-language dates and timezone conversion are unsupported. Server local date can differ by one day from a client in another timezone.
The UI is a minimal single-page client, not a polished product; no internationalization, offline cache, or mobile-native behavior.
Schema v1 has no migration path. Changing entities later needs an explicit migration or a new disposable database.
Concurrency is sized for one user; SQLite WAL and busy_timeout reduce but do not eliminate lock contention.

User decision points: confirm one-home scope, the default due date of creation day when no anchor is provided, latest-completion rollover for backdated entries, strict date-only input, and the absence of delete and defect-tracking features.
Restart durability may be described as an operator stop and start step in README; it was not run and is not claimed as verified.

items.title: Personal Project Board (个人小项目看板) - local single-user kanban board

scenario.name: Personal Project Board (个人小项目看板) - local single-user kanban board
scenario.audience: One person running a small personal project on their own machine (the board's only user), plus the engineer who implements and probes it. The user names the board, names the columns after their own workflow, writes cards with a title and a short description, moves cards between and inside columns, and reopens the app expecting the same board, column order and card order. The implementer needs an exact, dependency-free local contract they can code and assert against.
scenario.objective: Deliver a localhost-only, single-user, Python-stdlib web application that persists named boards, user-named ordered columns and ordered cards (title + short description) in one SQLite file, treats a card's column membership as the card's state (no separate status field), supports column add/rename/reorder and card move/reorder, shows every column's full card list with per-column counts, and reads the whole structure back unchanged after a restart. P0 explicitly excludes accounts, collaboration, a separate status field, WIP limits, notifications, time reports and automation, and those concepts are rejected at the API boundary rather than merely omitted.
workflow: 1. Operator starts the process with `python3 app.py --data-dir ./data --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765`; the data directory and the SQLite file are created on first run and the startup banner prints the local URL.
2. The user opens `GET /` (boards home) and creates a named board, optionally seeding user-named columns (for example 待办 / 进行中 / 完成) in one step; the board is stored with zero hidden default columns.

3. The user adds further columns, renames a column in place, and reorders columns to match the real workflow; the column order is stored as a contiguous 1..N position sequence and is always rendered left to right.
4. The user creates a card with a title and a short description inside a chosen column; the card is appended at the bottom of that column unless an explicit slot is given.
5. The user edits a card's title or description; editing never changes the card's column, position or moved timestamp.

6. The user moves a card to another column (this is the state change - there is no status field) and reorders cards inside a column; the source column and target column are renumbered to contiguous 1..N in one transaction.
7. The user reads the board surface: columns left to right, each column showing its full ordered card list and its card count, with the board total equal to the sum of the column counts.

8. The user restarts the process against the same `--data-dir` and sees the same boards, the same column order and the same card order, because every write is committed to `<data-dir>/kanban.sqlite3`.
9. The acceptance probe (one disposable board per case, deleting only what it created) exercises the same journey over the JSON API and asserts the zero-write behaviour of every rejected request.

capabilities: Named boards with durable local storage (create, list, read, rename, delete)
User-named ordered columns (add, rename, reorder, guarded delete)
Cards with a title and a short description (create, read, edit)
Movement as state: cross-column move and in-column reorder with contiguous renumbering
Board read model: columns in order, full per-column card lists and per-column counts
limits: 辅助试产，非严格G1/T08。

Runtime verification status: not_run. No target server was started, no HTTP request was issued and no probe case was executed while producing this blueprint; the acceptance criteria state what must hold, not what was observed.

Upstream status: not_run. The pinned Kanboard snapshot was read as source text only - it was not installed, started or exercised - so no upstream runtime behaviour, upstream database schema or upstream performance characteristic is asserted here.

Only the eight pinned upstream files were read; the rest of the upstream tree (routing, migrations, templates, tests) is outside the evidence set, so claims about upstream beyond these files are not made.

Restart durability is specified but not demonstrated: the probe cannot stop or start the server, so the cross-process restart check exists only as an operator procedure in README.md and is not claimed as executed.

The probe compares API-level shapes only; it asserts nothing about the HTML surface, so the accessibility, Post/Redirect/Get and focus requirements of the UI are reviewed by hand rather than machine-checked.
Drag-and-drop is deliberately out of P0: the UI exposes movement through buttons and a select, so pointer-only drag affordances, live drag feedback and cross-column drag previews are not covered.

The target stores no due dates, recurrence rules, assignees, labels, priorities, attachments, comments, checklists, activity history or archive, so the leaf's 'card detail' and 'standard capabilities' layers are absent by design in P0.
Deletion is destructive without archive or undo, so a mistaken board deletion cannot be recovered in this P0 build (decision D5).
The HTTP server is single-threaded and the probe runs sequentially, so concurrent writers, lock contention and busy_timeout behaviour are not exercised.
No authentication, TLS, per-board permissions or multi-user isolation: the process must stay on the loopback interface.
Column rename has no per-column history and card edits record no change log, so 'the position confirmed in the card's history' from the leaf is not implemented in P0.
The upstream MIT licence covers the pinned reference files only; no upstream source was copied into the target, and a file-level licence audit of the upstream tree was not performed.
